# Rules and process fixes

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
Three process fixes this session proved, each with the incident behind it.

PO-6 IS A SEARCH, NOT AN ACTION. Full record in docs/mistakes/M21. The rule
says "before adding an entry to any registry, open the file that READS that
registry first", and a session satisfies it by checking the registry it is
already thinking about. A new shipping tool here had to join FOUR registries
(pyproject.toml py-modules, tools/write_sites.json, the no-network allowlist
in tools/test_bm.py, and the prose count in SECURITY.md) plus clear a string
sweep in test_bm_store.py. Two were checked, PO-6 was reported as honoured,
and the gate found the other three at the cost of a full 27 minute cycle.
The reconnaissance that answers it in five minutes is in M21, with both of
the ways it was wrong when first drafted.

RUN THE GATE ON A COMMITTED TREE, ALWAYS. tools/test_all.py ends with a dirt
check over every TRACKED path and refuses to report green if any moved. It
cannot distinguish a suite's write from an author's uncommitted work, so a
gate launched over staged changes reports "REFUSING to report green. The
suites left these tracked paths modified", naming the author's own files and
saying something false about the suites. Commit first, then gate, then push.
This session also nearly repeated M20 by launching a gate with an untracked
handover pack in the tree, and killed it by PID after printing the target
rather than letting it produce an ambiguous verdict.

A SESSION-UNIQUE GATE LOG, AND ALWAYS --artifacts. PO-1's recipe writes to
$TMPDIR/gate.log, and $TMPDIR is shared between concurrent sessions on this
machine. Two runs interleaved into one file that contradicted itself inside a
single page. The per-run --artifacts directory was the only trustworthy
record, and the predecessor session omitted it entirely, which cost its
successor a re-run to recover failure text that was never written down.
The sentinel must also be session-unique for the same reason PO-1 already
says it must be cleared: a stale one fails toward green.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
